findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: Observed boxes of single use items including cups and napkins to be stored on the floor in the facility. Provide proper storage for the single use items. 750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Bleach solution in spray bottle was at less than 50ppm. More water was added to the solution earlier today and additional bleach was not placed in the solution. More bleach was added to bring the solution to proper concentration.

Maintain bleach solutions for sanitizing general surfaces at 100-200ppm. Use test strips to verify concentration of solutions. Check solutions periodically to ensure solutions are at proper concentration.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750.830g - Chlorine test strips were not available for checking sanitizer concentrations. Strips and a chart were provided by inspector for the remainder of the day. The Director stated she would purchase test strips by tomorrow morning. A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million. **Use the test strips every time a bleach solution is prepared for wiping general surfaces, and maintain the solution at 100ppm**

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text: 750.1300 & 1320 - Spray bottle of bleach solution was not labeled, and the concentration of the solution was over 200ppm (test strip turned dark purple to black in color). Bottle was properly labeled "bleach solution" and remade at proper concentration of 100ppm. Container and spray bottles of chemicals must be properly labeled as to the contents. Chemicals can not be used in any way that may contaminate foods or surfaces nor pose a hazard to people. Maintain bleach solutions at 100ppm chlorine, and use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Absence of a working thermometer in the small white refrigerator.
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.
